hash_note: The assignment pinned 21df6f7f and said 'await freeze or note the hash you read'. I read and hashed the head on disk: 23fec0e9 (revision 3, supersedes 8534b913). No freeze is declared for F2a in research_map.json frozen_artifacts. This verdict binds only 23fec0e9.
score_rationale: The class identity, family separation and the primary quantifier block are sound (P1-P5), but three critical defects sit in the artifact's core: the operative conclusion statement still quantifies over an undefined disjunctive domain (HF-1), the extension predicate the whole class is about is not defined in the document (HF-2), and the genericity block re-imports a matter-coupled phenomenon into a vacuum class (HF-3). Two of the three are in the conclusion/definition path, not in prose. This is fixable by one revision (propagate the single-domain statement and import the C0 sibling's predicate block with C2 values), hence revise, not reject.
hard_failures: HF-06 (single-class binding; critical): conclusion.statement_formal (line 209) still reads 'forall (s,delta) in D0, forall D in D_gen^{s,delta}' where D0 is defined nowhere (the document's domains are D1/D2/D3 at lines 66-76) and (s,delta) is exactly the regularity-pair binder that revision 3 removed. It contradicts quantifiers.formal (line 52), order_note (line 78: 'exactly one frozen data class and no regularity-pair binder, so the sentence is a single class statement'), data_class.regularity_class.demoted_alternative (line 118), and D2 (line 71). It also substitutes the all-data strengthening the file itself forbids (line 220). This is the same defect lead-audit reopened revision 2 for (review_history line 390): revision 3 fixed quantifiers.formal but did not propagate the fix to the operative conclusion block.

HF-06 (undefined class core; critical; A0 hard-failure taxonomy has no dangling-definition code, nearest is HF-06 because the statement's assumption set is incomplete): extension_predicate is referenced at lines 75, 76 (D3 = 'triples satisfying every clause (a)-(f) of extension_predicate'), 209 and 211, and acceptance_map R06/R14 (lines 410, 418) rely on it, but the document defines no extension_predicate block anywhere. The sibling C0 document does define it (schemas/af_scc_c0_vacuum.yaml:89). Consequently D3, conclusion.statement_formal and equivalent_standard_formulation cannot be instantiated, and the binding gate fails R17/R18/R18 on exactly this absence. Without the predicate neither the conclusion nor the tier-1 falsifier is well-posed.

HF-02 (class leakage; critical): genericity.excluded_set (line 155) lists 'fine-tuned threshold data of type-II critical collapse' - a matter-coupled model phenomenon - as a candidate member of the vacuum exceptional set, with no source in provenance (lines 328-369) and no transfer argument, while the file itself forbids matter-coupled content in this block (lines 172, 187, 236, 241) and asserts R12 clean (line 416). lead-audit coded this same pattern HF-02 at revision 1 (binding_note line 25), and revision 3 reintroduced a different matter-coupled token in the same block.
findings: P1 positive, no class leakage: conclusion_type scc_c2_future_inextendibility (lines 42, 205) is the rule_spec v1.1 vocabulary for AF-SCC-C2-VAC-GEN; no C0 conclusion token appears in an assertive block (lines 140, 144-148, 217-219, 229-238, 313-322); the frozen detector research_map/class_separation.py (sha256:c266dbceca87) returns no findings on the parsed C2, C0 and WCC documents, and runtime/bin/classsep_regression.py reports leaks 17/17 and controls 10/10 (FP 0, FN 0).

P2 positive, no WCC conclusion inflation: i_plus.role=assumption with in_conclusion=false (lines 190-192), visibility.role=not_in_conclusion (lines 197-202), forbidden_falsifier (line 201), and forbidden_strengthenings naming I+ completeness and visible-singularity content (lines 221-222); every occurrence of 'visible'/'completeness' in the file is inside a prohibition or an explanatory sentence, not a conclusion.

P3 positive, primary quantifier block correct: quantifiers.formal (line 52) has the order exists-comeagre G over D_w, then forall D over the frozen data class, then not_exists over proper future C2 extensions, with ordered entries and resolved D1/D2/D3 (lines 53-76), matching negation and negation_normal_form (lines 79-80). This is the revision-3 fix line 118 claims.

P4 positive, topology block complete: 4D (line 86), connected complete orientable smooth one-ended slice (line 87), I+/I-/i0 with I+ topology R x S^2 (lines 89-93), global hyperbolicity (line 94), MGHD maximality (line 95), forbidden closed and periodic slices (lines 96-98).

P5 positive, falsifier is two-tier and self-critical: tier 1 requires non-meagreness plus an exhibited extension (lines 276-285), tier 2 is labelled refutes_strengthening_only (lines 286-289), schema_falsifiers separate wrong-family falsifiers (lines 290-294), and line 285 states the load-bearing non-meagerness step is not machine-checkable; provenance marks three citations unresolved (lines 357-369) and declares no_source_establishes_conclusion (line 370).

F-4 major, cross-artifact data contract is not frozen: lines 109-119 and 133-134 claim the data_class is 'exactly the F1 canonical data class' and 'shared with F1', but F1 on disk (sha256:7a3e1f93f77c) marks its weighted indices proposed_by_F1_unreviewed (lines 191, 195), its data_class status partial (line 197) and data_class.weighted_norm unresolved (lines 198, 440); the C0 sibling on disk (sha256:e6b1af2bd692) freezes smooth-with-decay and declares the weighted Sobolev setting 'IS NOT this class' (schemas/af_scc_regularities.yaml:38). F2a is also internally inconsistent, selecting weighted H^4_{1/2+epsilon} (line 110) then writing 'H^4_loc/H^3_loc' (lines 133, 148). Transfer rule T1 requires an exact match, so no pair in {F1,F2a,F2b} matches at the reviewed revision and G-FORM's one-data-class criterion is unmet. F2a discloses the F2b half (lines 133, 424) but overstates the F1 half.

F-5 major, tier-1 falsifier is not a finite decision procedure (A0 evaluation_rubric.yaml:131): machine_checkable_steps (lines 279-284) offer 'sampled derivative checks' for C2 and residual tolerances for Ric=0, which are evidence probes, not decision procedures, and the load-bearing non-meagerness step is admitted non-machine-checkable (line 285). The artifact is honest about the gap, but the gate criterion 'falsifier is a finite, checkable procedure in the stated topology' is not met as written; relabel the probes or specify a decidable witness format.

F-6 major, binding-gate compliance is overstated at this revision: artifacts/formulation/tools/check_class_schema.py (sha256:000e09e46b2f) returns verdict=fail with R17, R18 (twice), R19, R22 and R27 on 23fec0e9. I verified each firing: R17/R18 (twice) are genuine and are HF-2; R19 is genuine (no class_contract_pointer key exists); R22 is a key-manifest mismatch that also hits F1 (I enumerated 153 key paths absent from KEY_MANIFEST sha256:8ce752b5d8ba, including the entire acceptance_map, and the checker truncates the report to six), so I do not charge R22 to F2a except as manifest-alignment drift; R27's printed message is a false positive on lines 52-65 because the gate looks for a binder 'G_' or a domain_id containing 'comeagre' while F2a names the binder 'G' and puts 'comeagre' in the domain text - but the all-data strengthening R27 is meant to catch does exist at line 209 (HF-1), which R27 never reads. The artifact's evidence_refs (line 400) and acceptance_map R01-R16 (lines 404-420) therefore overstate gate compliance at the reviewed hash. Mitigation: the gate binary (mtime 23:50) postdates the artifact (mtime 23:38), so this is a re-check obligation, not proof of author misconduct.

F-7 minor, the separation index F2a leans on is stale and uncertified: line 232 points to schemas/af_scc_regularities.yaml as the machine-checkable index, but that aggregator (sha256:c6bfda2bf3f5) claims canonical_gate: pass for the C2 component at 23fec0e9 (line 32), which is false against the gate I ran, and pins the C0 component at cb897b29 (line 37) while the C0 file on disk hashes e6b1af2b, violating the aggregator's own SEP-6 rule (lines 53-54: a component change invalidates the aggregator until re-pinned).

F-8 minor, assertive-block topology hedge and unbound k: line 99 says 'multiple ends are admitted only if declared explicitly; the primary case is one end', conflicting with the one-ended D2 (line 71) and slice_topology (line 87); a class-bound schema should not carry a second topology in an assertive block. Line 139's 'k is part of the assumption' leaves k unbound in the quantifier prefix; state 'for some fixed k >= 3' to avoid reading it as a second quantifier.

F-9 minor, coarse citation label: vocabulary_alignment.citation_status: verified (line 49) and provenance.citation_status: verified (line 327) coexist with three unresolved_citations (lines 357-369). The list is honest, but a downstream linter reading only the field would record full support; qualify the field (for example verified_for_PS1-PS4_unresolved_listed).

F-10 minor, stale self-review history: provenance.review_history (lines 391-395) still records revision 3 as sha256/reviewer/verdict 'pending' although F2a-review-17.json and F2a-review-18.json already bind 23fec0e9 (23:45 and 23:47). Update the block or label it explicitly as authoring-time state.

tests.test: semantic arm - can a C0-regularity datum or extension satisfy the C2 schema?
tests.method: read the acceptance predicate the test must evaluate
tests.detail: the predicate to evaluate (extension_predicate, referenced at lines 75, 76, 209, 211) is absent from the document, so there is nothing to run the C0 datum against. The only available separators are regularity.extension_regularity: C2 (line 140) and must_not_conflate (lines 144-148), which exclude C0 by declaration, not by a checkable predicate.

falsifier_test.conclusion: The falsifier did not fire on its two decidable arms; its semantic arm is blocked by HF-2. This review therefore records separation-by-declaration only and does not certify C2/C0 semantic separation.
